answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted counterparty diversity. An agent's identity weight grows only through deals with distinct, already-bonded peers, each co-signing a receipt. A lone operator can thus form only a thin thread of weight with itself, since the co-signer graph discounts self-referential receipts to near zero. To enter, a new key posts a vault bond unlocked only after seven unrelated peers attest real work. Every fake identity costs slashable capital plus seven separate reputations, not a free keypair. A fable spreads at no cost; a signed receipt cannot.
